title: Forces on two objects
target: Identify an equal-and-opposite interaction pair on different objects.
criteria: Name both objects in an interaction pair.
Place the two equal-and-opposite forces on different objects.
Explain why equal forces can produce unequal accelerations.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A person’s hand pushes on a wall. What is the third-law partner?
options: The floor pushes on the person.
The hand’s motion pushes on itself.
The wall pushes on the hand.
Gravity pulls on the hand.
cpa.guide: The interaction pair exchanges source and recipient.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Earth pulls gravitationally on a satellite. Which is the partner force?
options: An unrelated engine force on the satellite.
The satellite pulls gravitationally on Earth.
The satellite’s velocity.
The satellite’s weight on itself.
cpa.guide: Both forces belong to the same gravitational interaction between two bodies.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A rope pulls a crate right with 16 N. What force does the crate exert on the rope?
options: 16 N right.
A larger force if the crate accelerates.
Zero because the crate is heavy.
16 N left.
cpa.guide: The forces are equal and opposite even during acceleration.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Why do third-law partners not cancel on one object’s free-body diagram?
options: One is imaginary.
One force occurs later.
Their magnitudes are unequal.
They act on different objects.
cpa.guide: Each object’s diagram includes only the force acting on that object.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A 2 kg cart and a 6 kg cart push each other with equal force magnitudes. Compare acceleration magnitudes due to that interaction.
options: The 2 kg cart’s is three times as large.
Both accelerations must be equal.
Both accelerations must be zero.
The 6 kg cart’s is three times as large.
cpa.guide: a = F/m; the smaller mass has three times the acceleration.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A large truck and small car collide. Which statement separates force from acceleration correctly?
options: Mutual force magnitudes are equal; acceleration magnitudes depend on each mass and other forces.
The truck necessarily exerts a greater mutual force.
The car exerts no force on the truck.
Equal mutual forces guarantee identical total accelerations.
cpa.guide: Third-law forces are equal, but each object has its own mass and net-force account.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
